extraction.notes: Unofficial English translation published by the Personal Data Protection Agency; the speaker is recorded as the Agency because the text carries no decree or adopting body. Read in full. The law is extracted as an intervention with the provisions that establish the main rights, obligations, authorities, systems and EU alignment, as the brief requires; not every article is itemised. Left out as detail: the definitions (Art. 4), most procedural detail of consent, information duties, binding corporate rules, the appointment of the director, supervision procedure and the lists of misdemeanours. The law text states no adoption, publication or entry-into-force date, so event dates are empty; the publication year comes from the register. No passage concerns foreign workers or worker mobility, so nothing is tagged to Chapter 2. Art. 122 reads oddly as printed: see the note on item -0043. Second-pass check done (G3 condition 2).

items.stated_text: This Law regulates the protection of personal data and the righ t to privacy with regard to the processing of personal data, and in particular the principles r elated to the processing of personal data, the rights of the data subject, the position of the controller and the processor, the transfer of personal data to other countries, the establishment, status and competen cies of the Personal Data Protection Agency, the special operations for the processing of personal d ata, the legal remedies and liability in the processing of personal data, the supervision over personal data protection, as well as the misdemeanors and misdemeanor proceedings in this area.
items.summary: The Law regulates personal data protection and privacy, including principles, data subject rights, transfers, the Agency, remedies, supervision and misdemeanours.

location.section: I. GENERAL PROVISIONS > Subject matter of the Law

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: This Law is harmonized with the European regulation in the field of personal data protection, specifically: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Directive 95/46/EC (General Data Protection Regulation) CELEX No. 32016R0679.
items.summary: The Law states that it is harmonised with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679.

location.section: I. GENERAL PROVISIONS > footnote 1

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.extraction_note: A statement of alignment in the law itself, not an assessment of alignment.

items.stated_text: Protection of personal data sha ll be guaranteed to any natural person free of discrimination based on nationality, race, skin colour, religious belief, ethn ic background, gender, language, political or other beliefs, material status, origin by birth, education, social background, citizenship, place or type of residence, or any other personal characteristics of that person.
items.summary: Personal data protection is guaranteed to any natural person without discrimination, including on nationality, citizenship or place of residence.

location.section: I. GENERAL PROVISIONS > Prohibition of discrimination

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: The controller shall be r esponsible for, and be able to demonstrate compliance with paragraph (1) of this Article (“accountability’).
items.summary: The controller is responsible for, and must be able to demonstrate, compliance with the data processing principles.

location.section: II. PRINCIPLES > Principles relating to the personal data processing

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the c ontroller confirmation as to whether personal data concerning him or her are being processed, and, w here that is the case, access to the personal data and the following information:
items.summary: Data subjects have a right to confirmation of processing, access to their personal data and specified information.

location.section: III. RIGHTS OF THE DATA SUBJECT > Right of access by the data subject

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the c ontroller the erasure of personal data concerning him or her and the controller shall have the obligation to erase personal data within 30 days from the day of receipt of the request where one of the following grounds applies:
items.summary: Data subjects have a right to erasure, which the controller must carry out within 30 days on the listed grounds.

location.section: III. RIGHTS OF THE DATA SUBJECT > Right to erasure (“right to be forgotten”)

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: The data subject shall have the right to receive personal data concerning him or her, which he or she has provided to a controller, in a structured, commonly used, m achine-readable format and have the right to transmit those data to another controller without hind rance from the controller to which the personal data have been provided, where:
items.summary: Data subjects have a right to data portability, receiving their data in a machine-readable format and transmitting it to another controller.

location.section: III. RIGHTS OF THE DATA SUBJECT > Right to data portability

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: The data subject shall have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects c oncerning him or her or similarly significantly affects him or her.
items.summary: Data subjects have a right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, with legal or similarly significant effects.

location.section: III. RIGHTS OF THE DATA SUBJECT > Automated individual decision-making, including profiling

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.extraction_note: The provision does not mention artificial intelligence, so no TECH-AI code is given.

items.stated_text: The controller shall implem ent appropriate technical and organisational measures for ensuring that, by default, only personal data which are necessary for each specific purpose of the processing are processed.
items.summary: Controllers must implement measures ensuring that, by default, only personal data necessary for each specific purpose are processed.

location.section: IV. CONTROLLER AND PROCESSOR > Data protection by design and by default

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: Taking into account the stat e of the art, the costs of implementation and the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing as well as the risk of varying likelihood and severity for the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller and the processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including inter alia as appropriate: (a) the pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data; (b) the ability to ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integri ty, availability and resilience of processing systems and services;
items.summary: Controllers and processors must implement security measures appropriate to the risk, including encryption and the resilience of processing systems and services.

location.section: IV. CONTROLLER AND PROCESSOR > Security of processing

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.extraction_note: TECH-DATA is clear. TECH-CYBER is doubtful: the provision concerns the security of personal data processing, including processing systems, not network and information security rules as such.

items.stated_text: In the event of a personal data breach, the controller sha ll without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the personal data breach to the Agency unless the personal data breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.
items.summary: Controllers must notify a personal data breach to the Agency within 72 hours where feasible, unless it is unlikely to create a risk.

location.section: IV. CONTROLLER AND PROCESSOR > Notification of a personal data breach to the Agency

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: Where a type of processing i n particular using new technologies, and taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing, is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall, prior to the processing, carry out an assessment of the impact of the envisaged processing operations on the protection of personal data.
items.summary: Where processing, in particular using new technologies, is likely to create high risk, the controller must first carry out a data protection impact assessment.

location.section: IV. CONTROLLER AND PROCESSOR > Data protection impact assessment

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: The controller and the processor shall designate a data protection officer in any case where: (а) the processing is carried o ut by a state administration body, except for courts acting in their judicial capacity, which designated officer for other processing of personal data conducted in accordance with the law;
items.summary: Controllers and processors must designate a data protection officer, including where processing is carried out by a state administration body.

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: The Agency shall encourage the establishment of data prote ction certification mechanisms and of data protection seals and marks, for the purpose of demonstrating compliance with this Law of processing operations by controllers and processors, taking into account the specific characteristics of different sectors for personal data processing and the specific needs of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in order to contribute to the proper implementation of this Law.
items.summary: The Agency must encourage data protection certification mechanisms, seals and marks to demonstrate compliance by controllers and processors.

location.section: IV. CONTROLLER AND PROCESSOR > Certification

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: Any transfer of personal d ata which are undergoing processing or are intended for processing after transfer to a third country or to an international organisation shall take place only if the conditions laid down in this Law are complied with by the controller and processor, including for onward transfers of personal data from the third country or an international organisation to another third country or to another international organisation.
items.summary: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations, including onward transfers, may take place only under the conditions of this Law.

location.section: V. TRANSFER OF PERSONAL DATA > General principle for transfers

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.summary: The transfer chapter does not apply to transfers to EU or EEA states, but controllers and processors must notify the Agency of them.

location.section: V. TRANSFER OF PERSONAL DATA > General principle for transfers

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: A transfer of personal data to a third country or an inter national organisation may take place where the Agency has decided that the third country or the internatio nal organisation in question ensures an adequate level of protection.
items.summary: Transfers to a third country or international organisation may take place where the Agency has decided that protection there is adequate.

location.section: V. TRANSFER OF PERSONAL DATA > Transfer of personal data to third countries or international organisations

speaker.name_as_stated: Assembly of the Republic of North Macedonia

items.stated_text: In the absence of a decision pursuant to Article 49 paragraph ( 3) of this Law, a controller or processor may transfer personal data to a third country or an i nternational organisation only if the controller or processor has provide d appropriate safeguards, an d on condition that enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies for data subjects are available.
items.summary: Without an adequacy decision, transfers require appropriate safeguards, enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies.

location.section: V. TRANSFER OF PERSONAL DATA > Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards

items.stated_text: The Agency is an independent and autonomous state administ ration body responsible for monitoring the lawfulness of activities taken when processing p ersonal data on the territory of the Republic of North Macedonia, as well as for protection of the f undamental rights and freedoms of natural persons in relation to processing of their personal data.
items.summary: The Agency is an independent and autonomous state administration body that monitors the lawfulness of personal data processing and protects related rights.

items.intervention_as_stated: Law on Personal Data Protection (“Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia” no.7/2005, 103/2008, 124/10, 135/11, 43/14, 153/15, 99/16 and 64/18)

items.stated_text: Personal data are: - processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner in r elation to the data subject (“lawfulness, fairness and transparency”); - collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes a nd not further processed in a manner that is incompatible with those purposes. Further processing for archiving purposes in the public interest, for scientific or historical research purposes or sta tistical purposes, in accordance with Article 86 paragraph (1) of this Law, shall not be considered t o be incompatible with the initial purposes (“purpose limitation”); - adequate, relevant and lim ited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed (“data minimisation”); - accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date; every reaso nable step must be taken to ensure that personal data that are inaccurate, having regard to the purposes for which they are processed are erased or rectified without delay (“accuracy”); - kept in a form which permits identification of data subject s for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed. Persona l data may be stored for longer periods insofar as the personal data will be processed solely for archiving purposes in the public interest, for scientific or historical research purposes or sta tistical purposes in accordance with Article 86 paragraph (1) of this Law, subject to implementation of the appropriate technical and organisational measures pursuant to this Law, in order to safeg uard the rights and freedoms of the data subject (“storage limitation”); - processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security of t he personal data, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and agai nst accidental loss, destruction or damage, using appropriate technical or organisational measur es (“integrity and confidentiality”).
items.summary: The law sets the data processing principles: lawfulness, fairness and transparency, purpose limitation, minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality.

items.stated_text: Where the data subject has given consent for data process ing for one or more specific purposes, in relation to the offer of information society services directly to a child, the processing of the personal data of a child shall be lawful where the child is at least 14 years old. Where the child is below the age of 14 years, such processing shall be lawful only if an d to the extent that consent is given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility over the child.
items.summary: For information society services offered directly to a child, consent is lawful from age 14; below that, parental authorisation is required.

items.stated_text: Taking into account the state of the art, the cost of impl ementation and the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing as well as the risks of varying likelihood and severity for rights and freedoms of natural persons posed by the processing, the contro ller shall, both at the time of the determination of the means for processing and at the time of the processing itself, implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, such as pseudonymisation, which are designed with the goal of effective implementation of data-protection principles, such as data minimisation, and to integrate the necessary safeguards into the processing in order to meet the r equirements of this Law and to protect the rights of data subjects.
items.summary: The controller must implement technical and organisational measures designed to apply data protection principles and build safeguards into processing (data protection by design).
